text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The State Ownership Fund sacked managers of the Arctic refrigerator maker after the company recorded losses amounting to six million German marks.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania's current tax system does not allow small and medium-sized companies to develop properly, the newspaper says.
-The trade union federation Cartel Alfa asked for a cut in wage taxes.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Romtelecom telephone authority is expected to get a GSM licence worth $25 million on the 1,800 Mhz frequency.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- President Emil Constantinescu mediated disputes within the centrist ruling coalition over allegations that members of the coalition's junior partner Democratic Party (PD) have purchased houses illegally.
- Ex-president Ion Iliescu might resign as leader of the main opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), following a recent split in the party, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- PD leaders threatened to quit the ruling coalition if allegations of illegal house purchases were maintained.
- The mayor of the Galati port on the River Danube has resigned from PDSR to join a reformist group -- led by former Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu -- which split from the party last month.
- Heroin is the most popular drug in Romania, police and health officials said.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania, Moldova and Ukraine signed an agreement to boost tilateral economic cooperation.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- U.S. President Bill Clinton will address Romanians in Bucharest in the University square, a shrine of the December 1989 anti-Communist revolt, the newspaper says. Clinton is expected to visit Romania on July 11.

- German Chancellor Helmuth Kohl will support Romania for the "best possible solution" during NATO enlargement talks in Madrid next week, Constantinescu said after a recent visit to Bonn. ($ = 7,079 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
